title: Munshaʾāt-i Ṣāʾin-i Turka (correspondence)

date.ce: letters from ca. 1411 to ca. 1429 or later
date.basis: Letters are dated by MK by conjecture (letter 1: 16 Jumādā I [814] or 822; most others 'ca.'); collection order rough chronological; earliest copy MS Majlis 10196 was made 828-38/1425-35, so the marginal letters were copied in his lifetime

place: Isfahan, Shiraz, Yazd, Herat, Gilan, Mazandaran (letters)
addressee: amirs, viziers and shaykhs; Bāysunghur; Shāhrukh; Iskandar; Kārkiyā and Marʿashī rulers; Sharaf al-Dīn Yazdī (see the letter evidence)
occasion: a selection of his correspondence preserved after his death; the standard collection follows his career from Isfahan to exile
manuscript: MS Majlis 10196 margins (15 letters, ff. 51b, 122a, 139a, 148a, 153b, 160a, 172a, 188b); MS Majlis-i Sinā 316 pp. 1-34; MS Dānishgāh 2576 pp. 168-217; MS Malik 4029/6; microfilm 227
summary: MK counts 46 letters, fragments or notes in the standard collection (50 with the unique ones), of which only letter 27 to Amīr Fīrūzshāh had been published; they show his dealings with amirs, viziers, Sufis and the rulers of Herat, Gilan and Mazandaran, and are MK's main free-hand witness to his career.
